skill.hypothesis: In CSI1000-style small caps, short-horizon price pressure and attention bursts tend to mean-revert because liquidity is thinner and retail-driven overreaction is more common. A sparse contrarian signal should work best when recent returns and short moving-average gaps are extended, especially if accompanied by temporary volume expansion rather than durable trend confirmation.
skill.applicability: Most predictable in cross-sectional small-cap universes during range-bound or choppy regimes with elevated speculative turnover and weak medium-term trend persistence; less suitable in strong momentum-led breakout phases.
successes: Short-term reversal built from recent return extension plus short MA-gap reversion
Contrarian core strengthened by temporary volume surprise as an overreaction proxy
Sparse additive construction with mostly short-horizon terms for interpretable small-cap mean reversion
failures: Fails during persistent momentum regimes where volume expansion confirms information rather than noise
Weak in crisis/liquidity-shock periods when reversals are delayed and volatility dominates signal
Can underperform when medium-term trend leadership in small caps overwhelms short-term overreaction effects

Mild penalties on illiquidity and return-volume co-movement help avoid cases where volume is trend-confirming instead of noise-driven.
